memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast. On the first day remove
the yeast from your houses, for whoever eats anything with yeast in it from the
first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel. On the first day hold
a sacred assembly, and another one on the seventh day. Do no work at all on
these days, except to prepare food for everyone to eat; that is all you may do."
- Ex 12:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Alongside Passover came the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, no
yeast in the house at all.

Yeast works quietly. A small amount spreads through the whole batch of dough,
changing everything it touches. That is exactly why Scripture uses it as a
picture of sin's influence.

Paul applies this directly to the church: "Don't you know that a little yeast
leavens the whole batch of dough? Get rid of the old yeast, so that you may be a
new unleavened batch-as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been
sacrificed" (1 Cor 5:6-7). Notice his logic. He does not say "remove the yeast
so that you can become God's people." He says remove it because you already
are.

That order matters, or this becomes legalism. The blood came first, then the
clearing out. We do not purify our lives to earn salvation. We clear out the old
because we have been saved.

Practically, this means taking small compromises seriously. The habit you think
is contained. The attitude you think affects no one. Yeast never stays where you
put it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What small compromise have you decided is harmless?
2. Are you clearing it out to earn God's love, or because you already have it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, show me the small things I have tolerated that are spreading. Thank You
that I clear them out as Your child, not to become one. Amen.
